display.title: Chodesh Elul: The King Is in the Field
display.summary_short: On Rosh Chodesh Elul, Uncle Yossi explains how the last month of the year prepares us for a sweet new year, with the Alter Rebbe's parable of the King in the field.
display.summary_long: A Rosh Chodesh Elul talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Elul, the month of mercy, does two things: it brings the year to a close and prepares us for the coming one. Since 'all's well that ends well', we finish the year by improving ourselves, davening more nicely, saying brachos slowly and clearly, learning more Torah and giving more tzedakah than all year. On Rosh Hashanah we will ask Hashem for the most precious gift, life itself, because He is the King Who desires life. Uncle Yossi then shares the Alter Rebbe's teaching in Likkutei Torah: in Elul, Hashem is like a king returning to his palace who passes through the fields, where everyone may come out to greet him, and he receives them all with a radiant smile and grants their requests. Now that Hashem is so close, we should do teshuvah, start the new year with a clean record, and ask for the greatest request of all, Moshiach now.
display.lesson: In Elul Hashem is especially close and ready to listen; use the month to improve and to ask Him for a good year.
